summary.releaseRationale: Bundled OpenJPEG 2.5.4 is affected by OSV-2025-219 even though JP2/J2K is rejected by the current LocalDocForge media-type boundary. Bundled libheif 1.23.0 is enumerated as affected by the OSS-Fuzz memory-safety records OSV-2020-2308 and OSV-2023-1129 (introduced with no fixed release enumerated), and untrusted HEIC/HEIF inputs reach that decoder by design of the HEIF input feature. cryptography is constrained to fixed 50.0.0 because GHSA-g6cj-pr64-35w5 affects releases from 44.0.0 through 49.0.0; the affected PKCS#7 API is not used by pdfminer.six, but the project does not ship a known-affected component. PDFium 152.0.7947.0 and all enumerated version-unknown nested children remain advisory-unknown. Empty exact-version database results are not treated as proof of safety, and the Windows-native inventory is compositionally incomplete for other target platforms.

conclusionVocabulary.affected: An authoritative or official advisory source identifies the exact installed version as affected.
conclusionVocabulary.contains-affected-component: The component is an aggregate or distribution that contains an affected nested component.
conclusionVocabulary.contains-unknown-component: The component contains a nested component whose exact advisory disposition could not be established.
conclusionVocabulary.no-known-applicable-advisory: No advisory matching the exact version was identified in the named sources on the access date; this is not a safety guarantee.
conclusionVocabulary.unknown: Available provenance or advisory mapping is insufficient to reach an affected/not-affected conclusion.

authorityOrder: exact installed wheel license and notice files
moving upstream text only when exact source provenance is unavailable and the limitation is explicit
licenseVerification.exactVersionPolicy: A moving main/master license file alone is insufficient. Exact tag references are used wherever the upstream exposes a release tag; exact wheel/sdist evidence and a stated limitation are required otherwise.
licenseVerification.platformEvidence: Nested native versions and wheel notice bundles were inspected from Windows x86-64 / CPython 3.14 artifacts. Each other target platform requires equivalent wheel inventory and license retention.

embeddedSbomRuntimeBoundary.evidence: cryptography 50.0.0 Windows x86-64 wheel: cryptography-50.0.0.dist-info/sboms/cryptography-rust.cyclonedx.json and sbom.json
embeddedSbomRuntimeBoundary.inclusionRule: Include the cryptography-rust metadata subject, all 32 supplier records marked scope=required, and the separately declared OpenSSL 4.0.1 component. Include CFFI's physically embedded libffi as version-unknown.
embeddedSbomRuntimeBoundary.exclusionRule: Exclude exactly the seven supplier records marked scope=excluded (cc, find-msvc-tools, pkg-config, pyo3-build-config, shlex, target-lexicon, and vcpkg) and the nested cryptography_rust bin-target duplicate, which is a target representation rather than a distinct dependency identity.
embeddedSbomRuntimeBoundary.limitation: The supplier cryptography Cargo SBOM was generated with all_targets=true and therefore may over-approximate Windows linkage, including proc-macro crates. Required scope is retained rather than second-guessed. The pre-existing pydantic-core 2.46.4 embedded Cargo SBOM is not flattened by this S5 change and remains a disclosed inventory gap.

unversionedComponentPolicy.licenseTreatment: Retain the complete aggregate wheel notice or exact parent-source license header named by each record. A license conclusion may be recorded when exact source evidence applies to the physically embedded child even though the child's independent release version is unknown; the version limitation must remain explicit and no unrelated exact-version terms may be inferred.
unversionedComponentPolicy.applicability: The child is physically represented by, linked into, or named in the inspected Windows wheel's native aggregate. Reachability follows its parent runtime component or aggregate.
unversionedComponentPolicy.remediation: Obtain an exact child version and source/build provenance, re-run authoritative license and advisory review, and rebuild or upgrade the parent wheel when provenance cannot be established.
unversionedComponentPolicy.residualRisk: Without an exact version or source revision, affected/not-affected status cannot be established; aggregate notice preservation does not resolve advisory provenance.

limitations: Database results are a time-bounded snapshot, not proof that a component has no vulnerability.
GitHub repository security tabs may omit vulnerabilities published only through OSS-Fuzz, vendor trackers, or private disclosure; OpenJPEG is a demonstrated example.

PDFium security bugs are generally handled through Chromium/Google private disclosure. The installed wheel records PDFium 152.0.7947.0 with n_commits=0 and hash=null, so public release notices cannot be mapped authoritatively to this binary.

The components array contains versioned review records, not an exhaustive native inventory. Known unversioned PDFium, Pillow/libavif, and CFFI/libffi children are enumerated separately, inherit unknown advisory provenance, and make the CycloneDX composition incomplete.

The pre-existing pydantic-core 2.46.4 wheel contains an embedded Cargo SBOM with 103 components (101 supplier-marked required) that this S5 dependency delta does not flatten. Those Cargo records remain outside the LocalDocForge component array; the CycloneDX composition stays incomplete until every runtime wheel receives the same supplier-SBOM boundary review.

Native evidence comes from Windows x86-64 / CPython 3.14 wheels even though the Python lock and generated SBOM files are universal-profile artifacts. Other platform wheels require independent native inventory.
Platform markers mean a package can be absent on a particular operating system. Dispositions apply whenever the listed artifact is installed.

security.residualRisk: Concurrency cancellation and resource-exhaustion defects can still affect availability even without a published advisory.

components.name: click

components.name: colorama

components.name: fastapi
components.role: Local HTTP API routing, request validation, and response serialization.

security.applicability: Directly reachable by untrusted HTTP requests when `ldf web` is running; loopback is the default but nonlocal mode exists outside strict-offline mode.
security.remediation: Maintain token/Host/body/field controls and promptly update on any matching framework advisory.
security.residualRisk: Framework logic and dependency interactions may expose unpublished request-smuggling, validation, or denial-of-service issues.

components.name: h11
components.role: HTTP/1.1 protocol parser used by Uvicorn.

security.applicability: Attacker-controlled HTTP bytes reach h11 whenever the standard/full web server is enabled.
security.remediation: Keep Uvicorn/h11 jointly current and preserve request-size, timeout, concurrency, and loopback controls.
security.residualRisk: Protocol differential and request-smuggling defects may arise from interactions with Uvicorn or intermediaries.

components.name: idna

security.applicability: No application route passes untrusted document domains to IDNA; it is retained by the ASGI dependency closure.
security.remediation: Keep the hash lock and remove the dependency if the upstream closure no longer requires it.
security.residualRisk: Future API or networking features could make normalization issues reachable.

components.name: lxml
components.role: Native XML library used by pikepdf, including document metadata paths.

security.applicability: Malformed PDF XML/XMP metadata may reach native XML code through pikepdf; external-entity/network behavior is not intentionally invoked.
security.remediation: Keep lxml and its exact wheel current, reject malformed PDFs, and retain worker/resource containment.
security.residualRisk: The wheel contains native XML code whose lower-level library revisions are not separate records in this SBOM.

components.name: markdown-it-py
components.role: Direct parser for attacker-controlled Markdown in the Markdown-to-PDF pipeline; also retained transitively by Rich for local CLI presentation.

license.localVersionEvidence: Installed wheel metadata reports markdown-it-py 4.2.0 with sole mandatory dependency mdurl~=0.1 and preserves MIT files licenses/LICENSE (SHA-256 4a2260d6e2cd0f5a151a1e86dbfe7d3ed552b1e2beabf9941c1ba5c49cbce484) and licenses/LICENSE.markdown-it (SHA-256 792c48c5a849a15fdf9e37e8bcf9e6d1dd13b32b46c642a748a0a46a9919d473).

security.applicability: Attacker-controlled Markdown reaches this parser through md-to-pdf. The CommonMark parser enables only the built-in table rule; linkify and plugin extras are excluded, raw HTML is dropped by the conversion boundary, and execution remains inside the bounded job pipeline.
security.remediation: Keep the direct floor at markdown-it-py>=4.2 and the exact hash lock current; retain input, nesting, memory, worker, and timeout limits; do not enable linkify or third-party parser plugins without a fresh closure and security review.
security.residualRisk: A crafted document can still trigger unpublished parser complexity or memory defects; safe PDF output additionally depends on complete token-to-Typst escaping and subprocess containment.

components.name: mdurl
components.role: URL normalizer used by markdown-it-py for attacker-controlled Markdown link destinations in the Markdown-to-PDF pipeline.

license.localVersionEvidence: Installed wheel metadata reports mdurl 0.1.2 with no mandatory dependencies and preserves its combined MIT notice (SHA-256 7c605df6e28667a9603118e98274f64a49ce3eed0d26fccce9534a345e0ef955).

security.applicability: Explicit link destinations from attacker-controlled Markdown can reach mdurl through markdown-it-py. LocalDocForge emits link text and destinations into escaped Typst output but does not dereference ordinary links or enable fuzzy-link discovery.
security.remediation: Keep mdurl in the exact hash lock, preserve its combined MIT notice, validate and bound hostile destinations, reject unsupported schemes, and repeat exact-version review on upgrade.
security.residualRisk: Crafted URL normalization may still consume disproportionate resources or produce surprising destination semantics even though the conversion does not fetch ordinary links.

components.name: packaging
components.role: Version and requirement parsing dependency of pikepdf.

security.applicability: Only trusted installed-package metadata and application constraints are parsed.
security.remediation: Preserve the chosen dual-license terms and repeat exact-version review on upgrade.
security.residualRisk: Malformed local package metadata could still trigger parser defects.

components.name: pikepdf
components.role: Primary structural PDF wrapper; untrusted PDFs are opened through bundled qpdf.

security.applicability: Directly processes attacker-controlled PDFs; wrapper defects and bundled qpdf behavior are both relevant.
security.remediation: Keep pikepdf/qpdf current as a pair, reject parser warnings, and retain hard worker/resource isolation.
security.residualRisk: No exact-version advisory was found, but native parser memory-safety and denial-of-service defects may be unpublished.

components.name: pillow
components.role: Primary image decoder/encoder and owner of the bundled native codec set.

affectedVersionRanges: OpenJPEG versions v2.*, v2.5.3, and v2.5.4 as enumerated by OSV-2025-219
security.applicability: Allowed JPEG/PNG/TIFF/BMP/WebP inputs reach Pillow. JP2/J2K is not recognized by sniff.py and is excluded from images-to-PDF accepted types, so the affected OpenJPEG codec is bundled but not directly reachable through declared formats.
security.remediation: Use a Pillow wheel whose OpenJPEG includes upstream fix d33cbecc148d3affcdf403211fddc2cc5d442379 or a later fixed release; until then preserve JP2/J2K rejection and hard worker/resource isolation.
security.residualRisk: Format confusion, plugin changes, or future JPEG2000 enablement could expose the affected codec; other native codecs still process hostile bytes.

components.name: pydantic
components.role: Domain, configuration, report, and API parameter validation.

security.applicability: Attacker-controlled API form parameters and local CLI values reach application Pydantic models; raw document bodies do not.
security.remediation: Keep Pydantic and pydantic-core aligned and retain explicit application bounds.
security.residualRisk: Validation bypass or algorithmic-complexity defects can exist without a published advisory.

components.name: pydantic_core
components.role: Native Rust validation engine used by Pydantic.

license.exactVersionEvidence: pydantic 2.13.4 pins pydantic-core 2.46.4; the installed pydantic_core-2.46.4.dist-info/licenses/LICENSE matches the tag-pinned text

security.applicability: Attacker-controlled API parameters reach native validation code under application schemas.
security.remediation: Update only with a compatible Pydantic release and retain explicit size/range limits before expensive validation.
security.residualRisk: The Rust extension is native code and is not a sandbox; unpublished panics or resource-exhaustion defects remain possible.

security.remediation: Protect local configuration permissions and repeat review on upgrade.
security.residualRisk: A same-user local attacker can already influence broader application state; this package is not a trust boundary.
